name: MMStar
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples. The benchmark addresses two primary issues in existing evaluations: visual content being unnecessary for many samples, and unintentional data leakage in LLM and LVLM training.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2 [cs.CV].
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from current benchmarks (MMBench, SEED-Bench, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, MathVista) using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to filter out visually unnecessary or leaked samples, followed by strict manual review by three experts to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMBench-EN-Dev, SEED-Image, MMMU-Val, ScienceQA-Test, AI2D-Test, and MathVista-Mini, totaling 22,401 initial samples.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLM inspectors were excluded. The remaining samples were evaluated by 16 leading LVLMs to gauge difficulty and split into four levels: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11 hits), hard (4-7 hits), and tough (0-3 hits). Final selection of 1,500 samples was made considering both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B) with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer (meaning around 75% of LLM inspectors failed to answer correctly) were retained, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. All questions were converted into multiple-choice format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer should be based on understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts before manual curation.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The difficulty of samples was assessed by tallying hit counts from 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples, categorized into four levels: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). LLM performance on MMStar was verified to be close to random guessing, confirming visual dependency and minimal data leakage.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts conducted the manual review process.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as automated inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source), LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). VLMEvalKit codebase used for evaluation.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLMs' and LVLMs' training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar addresses critical issues in LVLM evaluation by ensuring visual dependency and minimizing data leakage, which helps provide fairer and more accurate assessments of multi-modal AI capabilities. This can guide the research community in developing better LVLMs and more reliable evaluation methodologies.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is constructed from existing benchmarks, with SEED-Image contributing the largest proportion (28.3%) of the final 1,500 samples, followed by MMBench (24.4%) and MathVista (23.0%), which may introduce distributional biases from those source benchmarks.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark currently consists of 1,500 samples which may not cover all possible multi-modal capability dimensions. The automated filtering relies on LLM inspectors which may not perfectly identify all visually unnecessary or leaked samples. The benchmark is static and may eventually be subject to data leakage as models are trained on more data over time.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) on multi-modal capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess 6 core capabilities: Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, and Mathematics. Two additional metrics (Multi-modal Gain and Multi-modal Leakage) are provided for evaluating actual performance gains and data leakage in multi-modal training.
